brief.conference_theme: The future of philanthropy: trust-based giving and community power

plan.summary: Find nationally relevant journalists and communicators who can moderate a discussion on trust-based giving and community power in philanthropy. Prioritize people with documented experience speaking or presenting at conferences or public events.
plan.location_focus: United States (national; virtual or any region)

angles: Philanthropy reporters and editors at The Chronicle of Philanthropy, Inside Philanthropy, and Nonprofit Quarterly who have moderated or spoken at sector conferences
Hosts and producers of philanthropy-focused podcasts at The Giving Review, Philanthropytalk, or Candid who have appeared as conference presenters
Journalists covering community philanthropy and trust-based giving at Stanford Social Innovation Review and The Nonprofit Times, with public event moderation experience

cards.name: Stephanie Beasley
cards.could_speak_on: Moderate a national conversation on how donor control, trust-based giving, and community needs shape philanthropy.
talk_ideas: Who holds power in philanthropic giving?
What donors can learn from nonprofits about trust and flexibility
How major donors’ choices affect community-led work
cards.bio: Stephanie Beasley is a senior writer and fellowship director at The Chronicle of Philanthropy, where she covers major donors and charitable giving trends. She previously reported on global philanthropy for Devex and spent more than a decade covering policy on Capitol Hill.
credentials: Dual master’s degrees in journalism and Latin American Studies from the University of California, Berkeley
cards.why_fit: Her reporting on major donors and giving trends, combined with documented moderator experience, makes her a strong fit to guide a national discussion about philanthropy and community power.

past_speaking.event: Women’s Funding Network Summit — speaker/facilitator listing identifies her as moderator
State of Nonprofits 2026: What Funders Need to Know

notable_work: Reporting on major donors and charitable giving trends at The Chronicle of Philanthropy

links.label: Women’s Funding Network Summit speaker page

cards.fit_reason: Direct philanthropy coverage plus more than one documented moderation or event appearance.

cards.name: Sara Herschander
cards.job_title: Journalist and audio producer; reporting for Vox
cards.could_speak_on: Moderate a discussion connecting philanthropy, nonprofit accountability, technology, and the communities affected by funding decisions.
talk_ideas: How philanthropy shapes nonprofit work and public life
Community power and accountability in giving
Technology, equity, and the nonprofit sector
cards.bio: Sara Herschander is a journalist and audio producer currently reporting for Vox on global systems of power, inequality, and technology. Her work has appeared in The Chronicle of Philanthropy, the Associated Press, and other publications.
cards.why_fit: She has reported on philanthropy and nonprofits and was listed as moderator for a panel at a UCLA Center for Philanthropy and Nonprofits conference.

past_speaking.event: Nonprofits and AI: Possibilities and Pitfalls, UCLA Center for Philanthropy and Nonprofits conference

notable_work: Reporting for Vox on systems of power, inequality, and technology
cards.fit_reason: Documented moderator experience and relevant reporting, though her current reporting role is at Vox rather than the Chronicle.

cards.name: Andrew Simon
cards.could_speak_on: Moderate a conversation about how journalism can surface community perspectives and strengthen public understanding of philanthropy.
talk_ideas: Journalism’s role in accountability and trust in philanthropy
How funders and nonprofit leaders can bridge divides
Reporting on emerging trends in giving and community power
cards.bio: Andrew Simon is editor-in-chief of The Chronicle of Philanthropy and joined the publication in April 2024. Previously, he held editorial and leadership-programming roles at Grist and Fast Company, among other media organizations.
cards.why_fit: His leadership at a national philanthropy publication and documented participation in a philanthropy-and-journalism roundtable offer relevant sector context for a moderator.

past_speaking.event: Philanthropy, Journalism, and Bridging Divides — Leading Locally 2025 roundtable

notable_work: Launched or co-launched Grist’s leadership programming, including the Grist 50 and the Temperature Check podcast

links.label: Institute for Nonprofit News speaker page

cards.fit_reason: Current role is confirmed by his publication, but the cited speaking event pages were inaccessible to verify directly during this check.
